node.name: Power, Interfaith Communities, and Relational Organizing
node.descriptionText:
Learn about the principles and practices of relational organizing used by networks of parishes, temples, congregations, and mosques across the state to create systemic change in Connecticut.

Members of Greater Hartford Interfaith Action Alliance (GHIAA), Congregations Organized for a New Connecticut
(CONECT), and Southeast Alliance for Interfaith Leadership (SAIL) share a belief that religious institutions are called to
do the work of justice. Their historical achievements include:

• Passage of one of the nation’s strongest Clean Slate laws
• Cancellation by HUD of three Section 8 contracts to Hartford slumlords 
• Abolition of welfare liens in CT
• Construction of affordable housing in New Haven

All are welcome to attend! Kindly RSVP so we order sufficient food.

node.name: Dialysis + Palliative Care
node.descriptionText:
Join us for a conversation with Dr Jeffrey Turner about dialysis.

Dr Turner is the Clinical Chief of the Section of Nephrology, Director of the Nephrology Clinical Trials Program, Medical Director of the YNHH Dialysis Unit, and Medical Director of Davita Branford.

Topics will include
* patient experiences with different forms of dialysis (hemodialysis in-clinic, hemodialysis at-home, and peritoneal dialysis)
* the decision-making process with patients
* dialysis as a bridge to transplant or as terminal care at the end of life
* why some patients decline dialysis
* the history of dialysis and the for-profit dialysis industry

Dinner will be provided.

node.name: YPA November Book Club: The Berry Pickers
node.descriptionText:
Love books or want to read more? Want to discuss books in a casual, friendly setting? Join the Yale Postdoctoral Association for the next installment of our book club on Wednesday, November 18th at 6:30 pm.

In November, the book we are reading is The Berry Pickers by Amanda Peters, a powerful and deeply moving mystery about a Mi'kmaq family fractured by the sudden disappearance of their four-year-old daughter from a Maine blueberry field.

Have a suggestion of what we should read next? Want to discuss the book but can't make it in person? Want to borrow a copy of this month's book from the group? Join the #book-club channel on the YPA Slack. (To join, go to https://join.slack.com/t/ypa-yale/signup, join the slack, select "Add channels", and search for "book-club". Reply to the pinned comment to suggest books for future meetings!).

node.name: Advanced Search Techniques
node.descriptionText: Learn skills to research like a librarian, including how to use "advanced search" techniques to find books and articles in Quicksearch.
node.descriptionHtml:
Learn skills to research like a librarian, including how to use "advanced search" techniques to find books and articles in Quicksearch. Join us for 30-minutes and get a step ahead for coursework and research projects!

Attendees will learn how to:

  • navigate to distinct resource types in Quicksearch (books, articles, etc.)

  • use filters (subject, author, discipline) to find more relevant results

  • identify Advanced Search features

  • broaden and narrow search results using operators AND, OR, and NOT

Audience: Undergraduate students. Graduate students are also welcome.

Students interested in this workshop might also be interested in “First Steps with Zotero” and "Demystifying the Literature Review." For individual support, reach out to your Personal Librarian or Subject Specialist Librarian.

Any student who attends at least 3 library workshops this semester will be eligible to receive a Yale Library tote bag! Learn more about the Workshop Incentive Program.

node.name: Food Systems Solutions Webinar 2026
node.descriptionText: This webinar “connects the dots” between France’s One Health Summit (Lyon, 7 April 2026) and FAO’s planned first-ever Global Conference on One Health in Agrifood Systems (2026), translating their goals and key messages into implementable actions for government decision-makers and national food systems leadership. To overcome current gaps, the session will explicitly anchor these One Health milestones in the post-UNFSS+4 implementation agenda, building on the momentum of the UNFSS+4 Stocktake and the Hub’s ongoing work to turn global commitments into practical results through partnerships, financing, and inclusive governance. Designed for policymakers (health, agriculture, environment, and finance) and National Convenors, the session will combine a narrative framed around integrated food–health–environment wins; practical policy recommendations on how to embed One Health frameworks in national food systems follow-up actions; and an “implementation toolbox” segment spotlighting the Quadripartite policy products that could support Convenors on cross-ministerial coordination on One Health.

node.name: YSPH Climate Change and Health Special Seminar: “The Changing Landscape of Scholarly Publishing: The View from an Editor’s Desk” with Dr. Joel D. Kaufman
node.descriptionText: The nature of publishing scholarly work is changing rapidly. There are many factors challenging authors and editors, including the growth of predatory journal practices, fast-moving advances in artificial intelligence, increasing rate of paper retractions, evolving open access requirements and processes, and the growth of paper mills. After a quick tour of the issues, we’ll have an open discussion of best practices in authorship and peer reviewer.

node.name: Postdoctoral Orientation
node.descriptionText:
Postdoc Orientation is your guide to a successful Yale experience and will highlight the most important things you need to know as you start your training. Orientation is not only useful and fun, it's mandatory! We offer orientation monthly, except for the month of December. Orientation is usually held on the third Thursday of the month from 9:45am-11:30am. Postdocs who arrive in December should register for the January orientation session. Please find the precise orientation dates on the webpage here: https://postdocs.yale.edu/postdocs/orientation-registration. Coffee and snacks will be served.

Please note: There is a separate orientation for postgraduates. You can find more information here: https://postdocs.yale.edu/current-postgrads/orientation

node.name: Daily Worship at Marquand Chapel
node.descriptionText:
Join us at 11:30am in Marquand Chapel for our daily worship.

Worship in Marquand often draws on a wide variety of inherited Christian traditions, with the worship of many denominations being represented. Beyond that, though, we also pay attention to the rising number of people in Western society who have a lively interest in spirituality but feel no connection to traditional forms of church and worship. So Marquand is also actively engaged in original, creative, and experimental forms of worship, both for committed Christians and for those exploring the faith.
